# hoop_sidecar (Resource)

Registers a sidecar with the control plane and owns the configuration it serves. The sidecar fetches that configuration on every heartbeat. Pass `token` to it as `HOOP_SIDECAR_TOKEN` next to `HOOP_CONTROL_PLANE_URL`, or `controlPlane.token` in the helm chart. Rules reach the sidecar through the `sidecar_targets` of `hoop_guardrail`, `hoop_datamasking_rules` and `hoop_ai_session_analyzer_rule`; `bound_rules` shows what reached it. A fleet whose pods identify themselves with a platform token uses `hoop_sidecar_service_account` and `data.hoop_sidecar` instead; the guide "Managing a sidecar fleet with Terraform" walks through both. Needs an Enterprise license, checked at plan.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Copyright (c) HashiCorp, Inc.

# A sidecar registered with a token. The token lands in state; pass it to the
# sidecar as HOOP_SIDECAR_TOKEN together with HOOP_CONTROL_PLANE_URL.
resource "hoop_sidecar" "payments" {
  name = "payments"

  configuration = jsonencode({
    admin = { listen = "0.0.0.0:19000" }
    audit = { file = "-" }
    listeners = [
      {
        name     = "appdb"
        protocol = "postgres"
        listen   = "0.0.0.0:15432"
        upstream = "appdb.default.svc.cluster.local:5432"
      }
    ]
  })

  # Reviews raised on the appdb listener go to these Slack channels.
  slack_channels = {
    appdb = ["C0123456789"]
  }
}

# A document kept as the YAML file you already deploy converts with
#   configuration = jsonencode(yamldecode(file("${path.module}/sidecar.yaml")))

output "payments_sidecar_token" {
  value     = hoop_sidecar.payments.token
  sensitive = true
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) The sidecar name, unique in the organization. Changing it replaces the sidecar and its token. Destroying a sidecar that a service account identity reached records its name, and an identity that maps to that name is refused until an admin clears it with `DELETE /api/sidecar-deleted-names/{name}`. A sidecar only ever reached by its token is not recorded.

### Optional

- `configuration` (String) The sidecar configuration document as a JSON object, in the schema of the sidecar config file: `listeners`, `admin`, `audit` and so on. `jsonencode(yamldecode(file("sidecar.yaml")))` converts an existing file. The gateway drops zero values from the stored document; the plan compares past them, so `""`, `0`, `false` and empty blocks are harmless. The exception is the first plan after an import, which shows them as added; that apply changes nothing on the gateway. Omit the attribute to store an empty document; the sidecar then refuses to start until one is set. Do not put `load_from_disk` here; use the attribute.
- `load_from_disk` (Boolean) When true the sidecar runs its own config file and the control plane serves only the license. A switch in either direction detaches every rule bound to the sidecar: rules imported from its file that nothing else uses are deleted, the rest unbound. The plan warns, the apply lists them. Switching it off also clears the stored document before `configuration` is written.
- `slack_channels` (Map of List of String) Slack channel ids per listener name, where that listener's reviews are posted. Every key must be a listener of `configuration`, with at least one channel. A listener left out uses the organization's default channel. Leave the attribute out to keep channels set outside Terraform; removing a declared value clears every listener it named.

### Read-Only

- `bound_rules` (Attributes List) The rules the control plane folds into this sidecar's configuration, read from the gateway. The rule resources own them through `sidecar_targets`; this is a view. The plan refuses a `configuration` change that removes, renames or re-protocols a listener named here. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--bound_rules))
- `config_state` (String) What the sidecar runs relative to the stored configuration: `applied`, `applying`, `not_applied`, `refused`, `not_served`, `restart` or `unknown`. Empty before the first handshake and under `load_from_disk`.
- `id` (String) The unique identifier of the sidecar. Rule resources reference it in `sidecar_targets`.
- `identity_issuer` (String) The issuer of the service account identity bound to this sidecar, if one reached it.
- `identity_subject` (String) The subject of the service account identity bound to this sidecar, if one reached it.
- `last_error` (String) Why the sidecar refused the last configuration, or why the control plane did not serve it.
- `last_seen_at` (String) When the sidecar last handshook, RFC 3339. Empty until it does.
- `token` (String, Sensitive) The token the sidecar sends in `hoop-sidecar-token`. The gateway shows it once, at creation, and stores a hash, so it lives only in this state. Empty on an imported sidecar.
- `version` (String) The sidecar binary version reported at the last handshake.

<a id="nestedatt--bound_rules"></a>
### Nested Schema for `bound_rules`

Read-Only:

- `kind` (String) `guardrail`, `datamasking` or `analyzer`.
- `listener_name` (String) The listener the rule is bound to.
- `name` (String) The rule name.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

```shell
# Copyright (c) HashiCorp, Inc.

# By name or by id. The token is not recoverable and stays empty.
terraform import hoop_sidecar.payments payments
```
